# Aurict

> Open-source terminal agent, AI coding assistant, BYOK mobile AI workspace, and fixed-income intelligence through Bondley.one. Aurict focuses on provider flexibility, specialist agents, local-first workflows, objective assistance, research, document generation, and terminal-native developer productivity.

## Core Pages

- [Aurict — Terminal AI Coding Assistant](https://aurict.com/): Open-source terminal agent and AI coding assistant with specialist agents, contextual skills, multi-provider support, and a BYOK mobile assistant.
- [Aurict Terminal Agent](https://aurict.com/terminal-agent): Detailed overview of the open-source terminal agent, its multi-agent workflow, command controls, MCP support, provider choice, verification model, use cases, and frequently asked questions.
- [Aurict AI Coding Agent](https://aurict.com/ai-coding-agent): In-depth guide to AI coding agents, the difference between agents and assistants, evaluation criteria, engineering workflows, alternatives, and adoption questions.
- [Bondley.one](https://bondley.one): Aurict sub-product for researching bonds, yields, and spreads through clear, comparable analysis.
- [Documentation](https://aurict.com/docs): Install Aurict, configure providers and API keys, connect tools, use agent workflows, and understand the runtime.
- [About Aurict](https://aurict.com/about): The Aurict manifesto, architecture philosophy, BYOK model, objectivity principle, and long-term product vision.
- [Roadmap](https://aurict.com/roadmap): Product direction across the terminal agent, mobile BYOK assistant, web platform, security workflows, and future AI research.
- [Changelog](https://aurict.com/changelog): Release history and product updates.
- [Privacy Policy](https://aurict.com/privacy): Privacy policy for BYOK workflows, provider keys, account data, and future policy changes.
- [Terms of Use](https://aurict.com/terms): Terms covering open-source software, BYOK responsibilities, acceptable use, security workflows, and disclaimers.

## Product Areas

- [Use Cases](https://aurict.com/use-cases): Real-world development workflows for refactoring, code review, testing, and documentation.
- [Code Refactoring](https://aurict.com/use-cases/refactoring): Refactor complex code with dependency-aware AI assistance.
- [Code Review](https://aurict.com/use-cases/code-review): Review code for bugs, security issues, performance risks, and maintainability problems.
- [Test Generation](https://aurict.com/use-cases/testing): Generate useful tests, edge cases, and verification plans.
- [Documentation](https://aurict.com/use-cases/documentation): Create README files, API docs, inline comments, and usage examples.

## Comparisons

- [Claude Code Alternative — Aurict vs Claude Code](https://aurict.com/compare/claude-code): Balanced comparison of provider flexibility, terminal workflows, agent architecture, permissions, verification, and the workflows where each product may fit better.
- [Aurict vs Cursor](https://aurict.com/compare/cursor): Compare terminal-native AI workflows with IDE-based AI development.
- [Aurict vs Aider](https://aurict.com/compare/aider): Compare Aurict's agent runtime with Git-focused AI pair programming.
- [Aurict vs GitHub Copilot](https://aurict.com/compare/github-copilot): Compare full terminal assistant workflows with IDE autocomplete and GitHub-native assistance.
- [Aurict vs OpenCode](https://aurict.com/compare/opencode): Compare open-source terminal AI tools, agent workflows, provider support, and extensibility.

- [Claude Code vs Aurict](https://aurict.com/blog/claude-code-vs-aurict): Comparison of Claude Code and Aurict for terminal AI workflows.

## Open Source

- [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/aurict/aurict): Source code, issues, releases, and contribution history.

## Languages

All public product, documentation, comparison, use-case, editorial, download, changelog, and legal pages are available in English, Turkish, German, French, and Spanish. Localized URLs use `/tr`, `/de`, `/fr`, and `/es`; English is served without a locale prefix.
